solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prophet's growth encompassing East

definitions.note: the prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt; the 's reads as 'is' linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the growth wraps round the compass point

parts.note: moss is a low green growth on stones and trees
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet's beard or some odd growth, wrapped round with talk of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known Old Testament prophet, who received the Ten Commandments, is called by this name.

clue.text: Organised Oldie match at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An elderly person's sporting fixture, perhaps a cruise-ship tournament, planned with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone methodical works in a systematic, orderly way, so the word is a synonym for well organised.

clue.text: Broad range of toasted crumpets

indicators.note: toasted suggests the crumpets are cooked and changed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wide selection of crumpets fresh from the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a whole sweep of possibilities from one extreme to another, a synonym for broad range.

clue.text: Rage about temperature in seat of power

parts.note: to storm is to rage furiously
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
T is the scientific abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Fury and heat flare up in the halls of government.
explanation.walkthrough: STORMONT is the building in Belfast that houses the Northern Ireland Assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont is the site of Northern Ireland's parliament and government, hence a seat of power.

clue.text: Members of clergy — second one's abandoned consecrated buildings

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the letter is dropped from the clergy word

parts.note: ministers are members of the clergy
the second I, one as a Roman numeral, of the two in the clergy word

explanation.surface: Clergymen, one of whom has walked out, have left their churches empty.
explanation.walkthrough: MINISTERS has two Is; 'second one' picks the later of them to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, so the plural means consecrated buildings.

clue.text: Ponder one of nine daughters

definitions.meaning: to ponder is to think something over deeply
the nine ... were the daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Think about one of nine sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to reflect; as a noun it names one of the nine goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: Groups of Southern courts

parts.note: quads, short for quadrangles, are enclosed courts in colleges

explanation.surface: Teams drawn from the tennis courts of the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Squads are small teams or units of people, synonyms for groups.

clue.text: Northerner second to support River Island

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the others

parts.note: the Esk is a river in northern England and Scotland
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A northerner places second behind a high-street fashion chain.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a British clothing retailer, which makes the two words look like one name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit person of the Arctic, the older term, is a northerner by any measure.

clue.text: Join in rising maestro's missing semi-octave

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read from bottom to top
the eight letters of the musician word with the apostrophe stand for an octave; losing half leaves the first four

explanation.surface: A conductor goes up in the world, short of half an octave, to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: MAESTROS has eight letters, an octave; dropping the last four leaves MAES, which 'rising' turns to SEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric or material are joined.

clue.text: Blue people — and where they might live?

definitions.meaning: people who are blue are down, depressed, so the downcast ones
a name for chalk hill country in southern England where people live

explanation.surface: Depressed folk, and the place one might expect to find them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England, such as the North and South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, it names the miserable; read plainly, it names English hill country where people settle.

clue.text: Caught in new impasse? Diversion needed

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the rearranged letters
new means remade, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Trapped in a fresh deadlock, someone needs a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IMPASSE to ESAPISM, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is diversion from reality through fantasy or entertainment.

clue.text: This religion if not caught at the outset could become fashion victims

indicators.note: could become says that this pool of letters can be turned into the other phrase
at the outset means only the opening letter of the cricket word is used

explanation.surface: A faith that, if left unchecked, could turn its followers into slaves to fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus IF, NOT and C ('at the outset' of caught) rearranges ('could become') into FASHION VICTIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivaism, or Shaivism, is the branch of Hinduism devoted to the god Shiva.

clue.text: Plump mother cradles one best

indicators.note: cradles means holds within, so the pair wraps round the numeral

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
mum is an informal word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A well-rounded mother nursing her baby is at her finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective for mother but is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or ideal condition, a synonym for best.

clue.text: Hot, he leaves after mostly low piece of music

indicators.note: after puts the shortened passionate word behind the shortened cow's sound
mostly means the cow's sound loses its last letter

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so these two letters go missing

parts.note: hot in the sense of passionate, vehement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks out, overheated, after a quiet bit of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb a cow does: MOO, shortened to MO. 'Hot' is VEHEMENT, which loses HE to give VEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement is one self-contained section of a symphony or concerto, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Old quest's for what apostrophes may signify

parts.note: missions are quests, with the 's giving the plural ending

explanation.surface: An ancient quest is meant to explain what punctuation stands for.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostrophe often marks letters left out, as in can't or o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe shows that letters have been dropped, so these gaps are what it signals.

clue.text: New ship's director, restricted by fat, put on small tropical tops

indicators.note: put on means placed in front of, so the abbreviation follows
restricted by means held in by, so the fat surrounds the other letters

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
the helm is the wheel that steers a ship

explanation.surface: A new captain, held back by his paunch, dons small shirts for the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun helmets, or pith helmets, are hats worn against strong sun in hot countries, so headgear for the tropics.

clue.text: Warren wept, upset with macho Aussie's attempt to pull a fast one

definitions.text: Aussie's attempt to pull a fast one

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Warren, distressed, cries alongside a tough Australian trying a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian idiom means to try to deceive or put one over on someone, an attempt to fool.

clue.text: Religion with standards shown by current philosophy

parts.note: pars are standards or norms, as in up to par
I is the symbol for electric current
an ism is a doctrine or philosophy

explanation.surface: A faith with high standards, set out by today's thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsiism is the Zoroastrian faith of the Parsis of India, so a religion.

clue.text: Article on legal discussion about engineers rejected in outer chamber

indicators.note: on means on top of in a down clue, so the article comes first

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
about means surrounding, so the discussion wraps round the engineers

parts.note: a moot is a mock legal debate held by law students
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A paper on a legal debate about engineers, turned down in the waiting room.
explanation.walkthrough: A moot is a mock trial argued by law students; 'rejected' turns only the moot-and-engineers part, MOORET, round, while the article stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteroom is a smaller room leading into a main one, an outer chamber.

clue.text: MPs, giving an example, mark Wales for devolution?

indicators.note: devolution suggests breaking apart and redistributing, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament use Wales as a test case for handing down power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving an example' signals that MPs are one instance of the wider answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament make the laws, so they are an example of legislators.

clue.text: After fighting me Roger is more friendly

indicators.note: after puts the rest behind the fighting word

parts.note: war is fighting
R stands for roger in radio talk, meaning message received

explanation.surface: After a scrap, Roger and I are getting on better.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmer in manner means friendlier and more affectionate.

clue.text: After midday sun improves

indicators.note: after puts the sun abbreviation behind the midday letters

parts.note: midday is the end of the morning, the AM end
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Once noon has passed, the sun gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: Midday is whimsically the end of the a.m., hence AM END.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or make better, so a synonym for improves.

clue.text: Major road's arrangement for faulty distribution

parts.note: the M1 is the main motorway north from London, with the 1 read as I
the apostrophe-s of road's supplies the S
a deal is an arrangement or agreement

explanation.surface: The layout of a motorway turns out to be badly shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway from London to Yorkshire; its 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is a wrong distribution of playing cards to the players.

clue.text: Pains of chaps in wrong trousers, ultimately

indicators.note: in places the men inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
chaps are men

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the garment word

explanation.surface: Men suffer in ill-fitting trousers, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Wallace and Gromit's The Wrong Trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Torments are severe sufferings, a synonym for pains.

clue.text: End in Outer Mongolia

indicators.note: in signals letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A terminus out in the remotest part of Mongolia.
explanation.walkthrough: Outer Mongolia is a byword for a remote place.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a limit or finishing point, as in a term set to something, hence an end.

clue.text: Quite a heartless battle

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is cut out

parts.note: the Somme was a major First World War battle

explanation.surface: A truly brutal fight without any compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Used for emphasis, as in that was some party, the word means quite a remarkable one.

clue.text: One who eats everything wasted more vino

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or drunk, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who devours everything is also drunk on extra wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore is a creature that feeds on both plants and animals, eating all kinds of food.

clue.text: Dark master sounding tedious

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

indicators.note: sounding means the next word is taken for its pronunciation

parts.note: irksome means tiresome and tedious

explanation.surface: A gloomy schoolmaster comes across as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Murksome is an old literary word for murky, meaning gloomy and lacking light.

clue.text: Endless trouble about this writer's works leaving everyone speechless

indicators.note: about means around, so the trimmed trouble surrounds the writer letters
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a mess is a troubled state
this writer is, said by the setter, is I'm

explanation.surface: Constant trouble over a writer's books leaves the audience lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MESS to MES, which goes 'about' IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimes are silent performances, so the audience and actors alike say nothing.
